title: Taiwan Assurance Implementation Act
official_title: An Act to amend the Taiwan Assurance Act of 2020 to require periodic reviews and updated reports relating to the Department of State's Taiwan Guidelines.
summary: The Taiwan Assurance Implementation Act requires the State Department to review and update its internal guidance on relations with Taiwan at least once every five years and to report those updates to Congress within 90 days of completing each review. Under current law, the review was required only once; this bill makes it an ongoing obligation.
brief: Converts the State Department's one-time review of its Taiwan guidelines into a recurring obligation — required at least once every five years — with a congressional report due 90 days after each review.

top_lines.headline: Recurring Taiwan Guidelines Review
subs: State Department must conduct a review of its Taiwan guidance — including the 'Guidelines on Relations with Taiwan' and any successor or related documents — at least once every five years
After each review, State must reissue the updated guidance to all executive branch departments and agencies
Congress must receive an updated report within 90 days of each completed review

top_lines.headline: Report Content Requirements
subs: Each updated report must include all information required under the original one-time reporting requirement
Must also describe how the updated guidance meets the goals and objectives described in subsection (b) of the amended Taiwan Assurance Act of 2020 provision

likelihoodReason: Signed into law on December 2, 2025, as Public Law 119-45. The bill passed the House on May 5, 2025, and the Senate on November 18, 2025.

items.main: Names the Act the “Taiwan Assurance Implementation Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Increased Reporting Regarding Department of State Taiwan Guidelines

items.main: Amends the Taiwan Assurance Act of 2020 to require the Secretary of State to review and reissue the Department of State's Taiwan guidance at least once every five years and to report to the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and House Foreign Affairs Committee within 90 days of each review.
items.detail: The amendment also expands the definition of the documents subject to review to include any successor document or related document containing guidance on relations with Taiwan, not just the original 'Guidelines on Relations with Taiwan' memorandum. The obligation continues for as long as the State Department maintains any guidance governing relations with Taiwan.

gaps: The bill requires the State Department to review and reissue its Taiwan guidance at least every five years but does not require the Secretary of State to take any specific action if the review identifies restrictions on U.S.-Taiwan relations that are not aligned with congressional findings.

The bill expands the scope of documents subject to review to 'related documents,' but does not define what constitutes a 'related document,' potentially leaving open which internal State Department policies are covered.

featured_quotes.name: Mrs. Wagner
featured_quotes.text: Mr. Speaker, it is undeniable that the People's Republic of China is the single gravest threat to our national security. It is undeniable that China has increased its destabilizing military activities in the Pacific. It is undeniable that China has its sights set on the full- scale invasion of Taiwan. The United States must not waver in our deterrence of this threat and our support for this nation.

added: Recurring five-year review and reissuance requirement for State Department Taiwan guidance
Requirement to report updated Taiwan guidance to Congress within 90 days of each review
modified: Taiwan Assurance Act of 2020 Section 315: one-time review converted to recurring at least every five years; definition of covered documents expanded to include successor and related documents

added: Added a short title: "Taiwan Assurance Implementation Act"
Review now must include reissuing the guidance (the "Guidelines on Relations with Taiwan" memorandum and related documents) to executive branch departments and agencies
Updated reports must now include all information required under subsection (c), plus how the updated guidance meets subsection (b) goals
modified: Review frequency changed from "not less frequently than every two years" to "not less than every five years"
Report deadline reframed to "not later than 90 days after completing a review" (was tied to the two-year cadence after the initial report)

Subsection (c)(1) insertion text changed to "and any successor document or related document that includes guidance on relations with Taiwan" (was "...disseminating such guidance"), inserted after "memorandum"
removed: Dropped the introduced provision requiring reports to identify "opportunities and plans to lift self-imposed restrictions on relations with Taiwan"
